review_notes: Reviewed the current top-level proposal.json in full, not the different proposal embedded in context.prior_result. The current proposal contains four owned-subject writes and no new links, entities, merges, or follow-ups.

Independently read both complete owned files in canonical and rendered form, all 64 subject records, all 134 baseline facts, all 26 outgoing links, functionality.md, and both complete disposition ledgers.

All four proposed writes are supported: fn_8003B044 does not write 0x34; fn_8003B9A4 uses a bounded rather than global attack-exclusivity scan; gm_8016AEEC returns timer_seconds rather than stage ID; and pl_8003891C provides broad explicit initialization without a proved complete-record reset.
The four proposed writes correspond to the four superseded baseline facts identified below. No additional retained-fact correction requiring a new write was found.

Verified foreign definitions and consumers for configuration loading, player storage, initialization, periodic qualification, running-distance means, debug display, results extraction, configuration thresholds, and Star Fox special-taunt gating. gm_8016B558 counts non-NA slots, whereas Player_8003221C separately filters on player state and a fighter predicate.

The periodic helpers' returns report sampling, not qualification. Zero intervals, repeated or missed boundaries, unsigned deltas, optional external storage, implementation-dependent unsigned-to-signed conversions, NaN, infinities, and pointer aliasing remain important documented contracts.
Rendered aliases were not used as independent semantic evidence. Section ownership, physical overlays, bitfield ordering, and register mappings are not proved by source syntax.

Foreign item-query definitions establish x674/x710 array selection and the It_PKind range assertion, but do not by themselves establish all gameplay identities or valid compiled indexing. The associated compound baseline claims remain explicitly deferred.
Acceptance is of the supported proposal with the independent dispositions below; it does not promote deferred baseline claims to established knowledge.
